stage_a.note: Smiling and upbeat delivery, clear positive engagement when asking for the deal.
Animated gestures and sustained engagement when describing the invention of the product.
Friendly, approachable demeanor and smiling at the Sharks during the introduction.

venture.description: A portable adapter that converts standard dumbbells into kettlebells for workouts.
venture.note: The founders present Kettle Gryp, a fitness accessory.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dan introduces himself to the panel and states his hometown of Missoula, Montana.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Andy introduces himself, states his hometown, and mentions they are the inventors.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dan explains that kettlebells are popular but expensive and take up a lot of valuable floor space.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Andy describes his idea to convert existing dumbbells into kettlebells, showing an early sketch drawn by a child.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dan explains that the device is a portable adapter allowing users to perform kettlebell exercises with standard dumbbells.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Andy lists several exercises that can be performed with the product, including swings and overhead presses.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dan states their ask of three hundred thousand dollars in exchange for ten percent equity in their company.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dan concludes the prepared presentation by asking the panel who is ready to invest in their product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dan invites the panel to pick up and examine the samples provided to them.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert handles the product and places a dumbbell inside the adapter.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dan provides instructions on how to properly insert the dumbbell and secure the latch on the adapter.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dan compliments Robert on his handling of the product.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark lifts the assembled product and notes that it is straightforward to use.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin lifts the product and jokingly shows Lori how to perform an exercise.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Andy notes that the product allows users to safely perform exercises that are difficult with a standard dumbbell.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin remarks that the product actually feels better and more comfortable than a traditional kettlebell.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dan agrees, noting that traditional kettlebells can crunch the hands, whereas their product has a comfortable grip.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks for the maximum dumbbell weight that the adapter can safely hold.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dan replies that the adapter is currently rated to hold up to fifty-five pounds.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori expresses positive surprise at the fifty-five pound weight capacity.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin questions the three million dollar valuation, stating they need significant sales to justify it.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dan confirms they have sales, stating lifetime sales of three point six million dollars and listing annual figures.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks for their sales figures for the current year of twenty twenty-one.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dan provides the year-to-date sales and projects they will finish the year at one million dollars.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond asks if Dan has a background in sales or is a hired spokesperson.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dan denies being a spokesperson, stating he was a Marine Corps helicopter pilot for twenty years.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond thanks Dan for his military service.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks what specific type of helicopters Dan flew during his service.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dan explains he flew Cobra attack helicopters during multiple deployments to Iraq and Afghanistan.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert then asks Andy about his professional background before this venture.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Andy explains he opened multiple ice cream stores in San Diego and ran them for twenty years.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks for the product's retail price and its manufacturing cost.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dan provides the manufacturing cost and retail price, noting it yields an eighty-one percent margin.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark observes that the product saves consumers money compared to buying separate sets of dumbbells and kettlebells.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Andy agrees, emphasizing that the product saves money and adds convenience for the user.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori agrees with the point about convenience and cost savings.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Andy notes that this problem is exactly what inspired him to invent the product.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks where the product is manufactured.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dan answers that the product is manufactured entirely in the United States.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin expresses approval of their domestic manufacturing.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks if they hold a patent for the product.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Andy confirms they have a utility patent protecting the closure mechanism integrated into the handle.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks how many knockoff products have appeared on the market in their four years of operation.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dan estimates there are two to three knockoffs but asserts they are not as successful.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks how the competing knockoff products are priced.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Andy explains the knockoffs are cheaper but of lower quality and less safe.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark points out their strong sales and margins, questioning why they need an investor.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dan explains they need a strategic partner to help them enter new retail marketplaces like big box stores.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks why large retailers are currently rejecting their product or not returning calls.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dan admits they are good at production but lack marketing skills to secure retail deals.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond suggests their strong direct-to-consumer sales indicate they are better marketers than they realize.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dan adds that they have sold over one hundred and six thousand units over the lifetime of the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dan jokingly updates the lifetime sales figure as the panel continues to handle the products.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin plays along with the joke about the increasing sales numbers.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks for the updated sales number in response to the joke.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dan provides another jokingly updated sales figure, adding two more units.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert praises the founders but states he does not see it as an investable business, and exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dan thanks Robert and jokingly compliments his hair.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark states the product is secondary and limited by the number of dumbbell owners, and exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dan jokingly tells Mark they will take him back if he changes his mind.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks the founders if they are familiar with his previous investment in a gym equipment company.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dan confirms they are aware of Kevin's previous gym equipment deal.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin offers three hundred thousand dollars for twenty percent equity, citing his industry connections.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Andy acknowledges Kevin's offer but states they want to hear from the remaining investors first.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark prompts Daymond and Lori to share their thoughts.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond notes that Lori has been unusually quiet during the pitch.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori praises their sales and notes the product's appeal to women, stating she will make a creative offer.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori offers three hundred thousand dollars for twenty percent equity as preferred stock.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dan counters Lori's offer, asking if she would reduce her equity stake to fifteen percent.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori accepts Dan's counter-offer of fifteen percent equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dan confirms the deal with Lori.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond jokes that they accepted the offer before he had a chance to speak.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Andy jokes back that Daymond should have acted faster.

decisions.note: Does not see it growing beyond its current state as an investable business.
It is a secondary product limited by the number of consumers who already have dumbbells.
He is in the space in a big way and can help them get to retail.
She can help sell to retail and a broader market including women.
Asks to lower the equity stake.
Founders confirm the deal with Lori.

record.notes: The video includes a brief intro and outro which are excluded. No major edits observed during the pitch.
